description: Production monitoring design for the validation agent. DESIGN ONLY. Every health-model probe layer has at least one metric and one alert. Metrics are computable from durable sources the platform ALREADY holds (BrokerAccountValidationAttempt, OperationalEvent, ProvisionerHeartbeat) plus a lightweight readiness probe — no new host agent required.

probes.name: agent_readiness
probes.source: backend-side signed NEGOTIATE (mgmt_client.assert_compatible) to :8791 with a bounded connect timeout
probes.notes: the ONLY sanctioned health probe — the agent exposes no unauthenticated /health; a connect timeout => UNAVAILABLE (validation_agent_unreachable region)

probes.name: validate_login_available
probes.source: NEGOTIATE supported_operations includes VALIDATE_LOGIN AND backend keyring provisioned

metrics.name: validation_queue_depth
metrics.source: single-flight: 0 or 1 in-flight + waiters (agent is single-flight); backend-side pending validations
metrics.notes: the agent processes one validation at a time; queue depth is really 'are requests waiting on the single-flight lock'

metrics.name: agent_supervised
metrics.source: corroborate agent_up with the GuvFXBetaAgent SCM service in Running state owning the :8791 PID (or a WinSW-injected start-marker in the NEGOTIATE response a bare launch cannot forge)
metrics.notes: adversarial (lens 1/2): a bare 'python agent.py' answers NEGOTIATE byte-identically to the supervised child, so agent_up alone CANNOT tell a supervised from an unsupervised listener — the exact Aug-5 vector. This distinguishes them.

metrics.name: agent_readiness_freshness_seconds
metrics.source: age of the most recent agent_readiness probe RESULT (timestamp), computed by the scheduler, not by the probe value
metrics.notes: dead-man's-switch (lens 3): every agent-down signal is conditioned on the probe running; if the probe itself dies, nothing updates agent_up. This detects a stalled probe.

metrics.name: oldest_inflight_validation_seconds
metrics.source: single-flight lock-held duration / oldest in-flight VALIDATE_LOGIN age
metrics.notes: wedge detection (lens 2/3): a validation that holds the single-flight lock and never completes leaves NEGOTIATE green (HEALTHY) while no validation can run. NEGOTIATE is a shallow probe (HTTP+auth+manifest), not proof a validation completes.

metrics.name: validation_total_latency_p95_ms
metrics.source: validation_timeline duration_ms distribution over the window
metrics.notes: latency-creep SLO (lens 3): agent_transport drifting toward the 10s connect timeout or MT5-init drift is caught BEFORE it becomes a hard timeout.

metrics.name: validation_busy_rate
metrics.notes: lens 3: validation_busy is the single-flight-busy symptom of a wedge; it must map to a metric so a busy-dominated window pages.

latency_breakdown.source: transport round-trip; a ~10s value == the connect timeout (agent unreachable)

alerts.name: agent_crash_loop
alerts.condition: agent_restart_total increments >= N within M minutes (source: supervisor restart telemetry AND/OR readiness probe up->down->up transitions — the latter is backend-computable and catches sub-cadence loops)

alerts.name: agent_unsupervised_listener
alerts.condition: agent_up == 1 while agent_supervised == 0 (something answers :8791 but it is NOT the supervised service)

alerts.name: readiness_probe_stale
alerts.condition: agent_readiness_freshness_seconds > K x probe_cadence (the prober itself has stalled — treat as agent-down)

alerts.name: validation_wedged
alerts.condition: oldest_inflight_validation_seconds > max_expected (~login_timeout_ms+grace) OR validation_busy_rate high while NEGOTIATE green

alerts.name: validation_latency_creep
alerts.condition: validation_total_latency_p95_ms breaches the SLO before a hard timeout

support_timeline_integration.reuse: trading/validation_timeline (the support timeline UI, stages + operator summary) and operational_events (WP5 VALIDATION projection)
support_timeline_integration.note: a validation_agent_unreachable/timeout attempt already localises to the transport layer in the timeline; the monitoring alerts link to the same correlation ids so an alert opens directly onto the support timeline for that attempt
